summary: This is a clean m<=8 router-only shape gate onto the landed restack (b99b1dd), and the per-shape router rows can be read without a companion. The m=1 claim is overstated: -8.7% is measured against old master (5.73 us), and against the restack's 5.38 us the cluster's 5.24 us is only -2.6%, close to the 1.5% noise. The headline cannot move outside its CI, so judge the run on the router decode_1 and verify_1 rows only.
justification: The mechanism holds up, but it is not the one the hypothesis states. In dc5d03c4 the cluster kernel itself is SLOWER than the restack's Triton kernel. router_kernel<8,8> profiles at 3.6 us (m=1) and 4.3 us (m=8), against _router_swapab_kernel at 3.1 / 3.0 us plus a 0.7-0.8 us memset node. The row still drops (5.24 vs 5.38, 5.08 vs 5.47) because a single graph node with torch.empty replaces the memset-plus-kernel pair, and each node costs about 1 us in a cold-L2 replay. So the gain comes from removing a node, not from a faster stream. That is plausible on H200, and the m=8 row is real (-0.39 us, per-shape speedup 5.18 vs 4.80, err ~20 ns). The two runs being compared were built on different bases (dc5d03c4 on 8b9ad43, the restack on b99b1dd), but SGLang's baselines agree within 1% (10432 vs 10368 ns, 26320 vs 26240 ns), so the cross-run row comparison is acceptable. Weakest link: the decode_1 m=1 expectation. The quoted -8.7% / z -16 is against old master's 5.73 us; against the restack it is 5.24 vs 5.38 = -2.6%, barely above the 1.5% per-shape noise threshold, so a re-measure could easily land flat. Second weakness: headline impact. Router decode_1 and verify_1 are ~5.4 us of ~48-49 us loads (weight 62 each), so 0.14 + 0.39 us is about +0.3% and +0.8% on two of six loads, about +0.18% geomean. Expect roughly 1.2237 against a CI of +/-1.5%. The headline will read within-ci whatever happens, and promotion has to rest on the router rows. Both rows remain 2.8-2.9x off the 1.75-1.78 us floor. The expected directions (router m=1/m=8 faster, everything else flat) are consistent with the code path: only router m in 1..8 changes.
confounders: bf16-restack-m16-swapab-router-swapab-m32 (landed b99b1dd): it is the incumbent being displaced at m<=8 (_router_swapab_kernel plus the torch.zeros memset), so the change is defined relative to it. That makes it the comparison, not a confound. If its swap-AB router were ever made memset-free, most of this hypothesis's margin would disappear, because the cluster kernel's own time is higher (3.6/4.3 us vs 3.1/3.0 us). Judge against the restack's rows 5.38/5.47 (job 1e90292c7b954d96), not against master-era numbers.

router-triton-hilo-fused-control-splitk-all-m, router-hilo-at-m8, sglang-gemm-dispatch-parity: superseded at m<=8 by the restack. They only set the hi/lo [256, 8192] bf16 row-major layout that the cluster kernel reads, and that layout is unchanged in b99b1dd, so there is no interaction.

bf16-m32-swapab-wgmma-triton, bf16-shape-gated-triton-winners-combo: these change other layers only. Per-shape graphs are timed separately, so the only interaction is about 40 s more prepare/compile time inside the 10-minute budget. The non-router losses in dc5d03c4 (qkv/o 5-9% slower) came from its 8b9ad43 base lacking the restack, NOT from the cluster kernel. Here those rows must come back flat, and if they do not, the run did not build on the restack.
interference: No companions are needed. The change is a pure shape gate (router, 1 <= m <= 8, n == 256) inside the restack's kernel_fn, and the profile names a different kernel on exactly the two target rows. A gain or loss on router decode_1/verify_1 is therefore attributable to the swap of swapab+memset for cluster, and every other row is a built-in null control: if any non-router row moves beyond noise, the build is wrong, not the hypothesis. Reverting the restack (ab-revert) would only re-measure dc5d03c4. The informative follow-up is a different hypothesis, not a companion: a memset-free swap-AB router at m<=8 (e.g. SPLIT_K reduction in-kernel or a single-CTA-per-column variant with torch.empty) to test whether node removal alone captures the gain without a load_inline CUDA kernel. That would not be needed to read this run.
rules_flags: None blocking. The hi+lo bf16 pair with fp32 accumulation at m<=8 is already what master runs at m=1/8 (router-hilo-at-m8 landed and passes the 1e-4 router bound and the one-hot 0.1% rows). TASK permits the hi+lo split for the router weights without an m restriction.

The gate must branch only on shape, cfg, stride, alignment and a prepare() constant set from synthetic data. Keep the source branch's preconditions (bf16 dtype, x.stride(1)==1, x.stride(0)%8==0, 16 B alignment) as well as the hypothesis's 1<=m<=8 and n==256. Never branch on values.

Do not port the source branch's mode=0 diagnostic (no DSMEM reduce, wrong result). If it is ported, it must stay unreachable from kernel_fn. All synchronize() calls, prints, the 256 MB L2-flush buffer and the self-check stay inside prepare().
load_inline compiles in-process; no subprocess or network is used. Keep TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST set and restored in finally, as in the source.
open_questions: Port faithfully: the source used state['router_cluster'] (NT bucket -> cluster size, 0 = fallback) plus a cudaOccupancyMaxActiveClusters gate (>=16 for CS=8). The hypothesis says 'router_cluster_ok' and 'compile only NT=8'. Keep the occupancy check and fall back to the restack's swapab when CS=8 NT=8 reports fewer than 16 active clusters. If the CS=4 variant is dropped, say so in the implementation notes.

Insert the hook after _router_prepare in prepare() so router_stages exists, and have the self-check compare against x.double() @ router.double().T, the same bounds as the source (rel L2 <= 2e-5, worst row <= 1e-4, one-hot exact vs hi+lo, run 2 bit-identical). m in {1, 5, 8} matches the gate. The m=9 outlier test stays on swapab.

Kill or promote on verify_1 m=8 above all (expected -7%). Treat decode_1 m=1 as a success only if its per-shape speedup beats the restack's 1.925 by more than 1.5% (above ~1.954). A 5.30-5.38 us row is a tie, not a loss.

At harvest, confirm in the profile: router_kernel<8,8> on router decode_1/verify_1 with no vectorized_elementwise (memset) node; _router_swapab_kernel on router decode_16/decode_32; _router_hilo_kernel on m=128/256; _bf16_swapab_kernel on the restack's bf16 rows. Also confirm qkv_gate decode_1 is near 12.2 us and not 13.5 us; 13.5 would mean the build was on pre-restack master, as in the nine 03:41Z mis-builds.

Why is the cluster kernel 3.6-4.3 us when swapab runs at 3.0-3.1 us? Cluster launch and scheduling cost and the DSMEM double barrier.cluster are likely causes. If this lands, the next stage should attack the kernel's own time, because the node saving has already been banked.
